from.place: Proof, first paragraph of lem-exc-dvr-galois.proof.md: 'The equality between degree and ramification index used here follows from the length of the finite free integral closure modulo a uniformizer'; the general norm/order formula behind this length calculation, Stacks Tag 02MJ.

title: Restriction of scalars length for a semilocal algebra
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism to a commutative ring whose set $X$ of maximal ideals is finite. Suppose every $\mathfrak q\in X$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$ and the induced field extension $k\to B/\mathfrak q$ has finite dimension $f_{\mathfrak q}=[B/\mathfrak q:k]$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Let $M$ be a $B$-module of finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. For $\mathfrak q\in X$ write $B_{\mathfrak q}$ for the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $M_{\mathfrak q}=(B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}M$ for module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $M$ has finite length over $A$ by restriction of scalars and $$\mathrm{length}_A(M)=\sum_{\mathfrak q\in X}f_{\mathfrak q}\,\mathrm{length}_{B_{\mathfrak q}}(M_{\mathfrak q}).$$

source.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), statement and its simple-factor filtration proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-length-module-simple-filtration] with $R=B$ to obtain a finite filtration $0=M_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq M_r=M$ with simple factors $Q_j=M_j/M_{j-1}$ for $1\le j\le r$. If $r=0$, every sum over factors below is empty. We will compute both sides of the desired equality from this one filtration; no decomposition of $B$ or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), first sentence of proof; Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces), part (2).

proof.text: For each simple $Q_j$ [def-weil-pbc-simple-module], choose $0\ne x_j\in Q_j$. The nonzero submodule $Bx_j$ is all of $Q_j$, so with $\mathfrak q_j=\{b\in B:bx_j=0\}$ the map $B/\mathfrak q_j\to Q_j$, $\bar b\mapsto bx_j$, is a well-defined bijective $B$-linear map. The ideal $\mathfrak q_j$ is proper; if $b\notin\mathfrak q_j$, simplicity gives $B(bx_j)=Q_j$, hence some $c\in B$ satisfies $cbx_j=x_j$ and $cb-1\in\mathfrak q_j$. Thus every nonzero class in $B/\mathfrak q_j$ is invertible, so this quotient is a field and $\mathfrak q_j$ is maximal, belonging to $X$. This proves directly the simple-factor identification used in the source.

source.place: Tag 00J2 (lemma-characterize-length-1), proof of (1) implies (3); Tag 02M0, second sentence of proof.

proof.text: For $\mathfrak q\in X$ put $L_{\mathfrak q}=B/\mathfrak q$. Since $\mathfrak q$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$, its $A$-action factors through $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Choose a $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_{f_{\mathfrak q}}$ of $L_{\mathfrak q}$, using its assumed finite dimension [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and set $V_i=\operatorname{span}_k(e_1,\ldots,e_i)$. These are $A$-submodules, and the coefficient of $e_i$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $V_i/V_{i-1}\cong k$. The $A$-module $k$ has length one: if an $A$-submodule contains $0\ne u\in k$, then for any $v\in k$ a lift in $A$ of $v/u$ multiplies $u$ to $v$, so that submodule is all of $k$. Thus its submodule lattice has exactly $0$ and $k$, and the definition of length [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives length one. The zero module has length zero by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 00IY (lemma-dimension-is-length), finite-dimensional case, with Tag 00IX (lemma-length-independent), proof; basis-flag expansion of the residue-field calculation in Tag 02M0.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to $0\to V_{i-1}\to V_i\to k\to0$ in the flag of step 3. Starting from $V_0=0$, induction gives $\mathrm{length}_A(V_i)=i$, and hence $\mathrm{length}_A(L_{\mathfrak q})=f_{\mathfrak q}<\infty$. The $B$-linear isomorphism in step 2 is also $A$-linear and carries submodule chains bijectively, so $\mathrm{length}_A(Q_j)=f_{\mathfrak q_j}$. Each sequence $0\to M_{j-1}\to M_j\to Q_j\to0$ remains short exact after restricting to $A$, since the underlying maps, their kernels and their images are unchanged. Repeated application of the cited additivity theorem, starting from $M_0=0$, gives $\mathrm{length}_A(M)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}f_{\mathfrak q_j}<\infty$. This proves the finiteness clause without presupposing finite $A$-length.

source.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), final two sentences of proof; Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive).

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in X$. Compute the localization of a simple factor using the fractions in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and the ring fractions in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\mathfrak q_j\ne\mathfrak q$, choose $a\in\mathfrak q_j\setminus\mathfrak q$ (distinct maximal ideals cannot contain one another). This $a$ annihilates $Q_j$ but is inverted at $\mathfrak q$, so every fraction in $(Q_j)_{\mathfrak q}$ is zero by the fraction equality criterion. If $\mathfrak q_j=\mathfrak q$, step 2 identifies $Q_j$ with $L_{\mathfrak q}$; the maps $z/s\mapsto\bar s^{-1}z$ and $z\mapsto z/1$ are inverse $B_{\mathfrak q}$-linear maps $(L_{\mathfrak q})_{\mathfrak q}\cong L_{\mathfrak q}$. They are well-defined by the fraction equality criterion, since every denominator has nonzero, hence invertible, image in the field $L_{\mathfrak q}$. The action map $B_{\mathfrak q}\to L_{\mathfrak q}$ is surjective, already on fractions $b/1$. Consequently any nonzero $B_{\mathfrak q}$-submodule of $L_{\mathfrak q}$ contains every element (multiply a nonzero element $u$ by a lift of $v/u$). Its length is therefore one, while the zero factor has length zero, by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Thus $\mathrm{length}_{B_{\mathfrak q}}((Q_j)_{\mathfrak q})$ is $1$ if $\mathfrak q_j=\mathfrak q$ and $0$ otherwise.

source.place: Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces), part (4), last displayed formula and omitted reader calculation in its proof, expanded here.

proof.text: Localize each short exact sequence $0\to M_{j-1}\to M_j\to Q_j\to0$ at the multiplicative subset $B\setminus\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] to its three consecutive pairs (including the zero endpoints); localization of zero is zero by fractions. This yields $0\to(M_{j-1})_{\mathfrak q}\to(M_j)_{\mathfrak q}\to(Q_j)_{\mathfrak q}\to0$. The maps are $B_{\mathfrak q}$-linear by their fraction formulas, so [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] applies over $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Using step 5 and induction on $j$ gives $\mathrm{length}_{B_{\mathfrak q}}(M_{\mathfrak q})=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\mathbf 1_{\mathfrak q_j=\mathfrak q}=\#\{j:1\le j\le r,\ \mathfrak q_j=\mathfrak q\}$. In particular these local lengths are finite. The localized filtration need not be strict; length additivity applies to these short exact sequences even when a factor is zero.

source.place: Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces), proof of part (4); Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive).

proof.text: Every $\mathfrak q_j$ lies in the finite set $X$, so partitioning the finite set of indices $1,\ldots,r$ by $\mathfrak q_j$ gives $\sum_{j=1}^{r}f_{\mathfrak q_j}=\sum_{\mathfrak q\in X}f_{\mathfrak q}\#\{j:\mathfrak q_j=\mathfrak q\}$. Substitute the expressions from steps 4 and 6 to obtain the asserted weighted localization formula. For $M=0$ the empty filtration gives zero on both sides. If $B$ is the zero ring, any unital $B$-module is zero and $X$ is empty, giving the same equality; the argument therefore does not require an unstated nonzero-ring hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), conclusion from additivity and Tag 00J3 (4); finite regrouping and zero cases written out.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02M0 (lemma-pushdown-module), proof, with its cited Tags 00J3, 00J2, 00IY, 00IX and 00IV; explicit basis flags and localized simple-factor calculations fill out the source.
